transposition: Horn in F: concert pitch is a perfect fifth below the written pitch. Source system 7 (printed measure 37 onward) shows treble clef with 8 below; the written staff-position pitches are retained and this octave clef mark is separately recorded for sounding interpretation.
clef: Treble/G clef throughout; a small 8 below is printed from system 7 / m37. No key signature was detected at page start; subsequent pitches use source-printed accidentals.
key_signature: none at page start (source visual review); do not infer a key signature from the orchestral work title.
measure_mapping: Audiveris MusicXML sequence agrees with printed sparse bar numerals; measure numbers below are sequential source-measure candidates 1–51.
review_method: Audiveris 5.11 MusicXML used as a candidate only. Every notehead location is bound to the original 380dpi source image using the Audiveris source-coordinate bounds. Pitch spelling/octave is independently recomputed from the source head center and treble staff geometry, then compared with MusicXML. Accidental symbols and cue source are retained as review fields; notehead-size reductions are flagged.
unresolved: Three low-grade OMR head detections (m1 n05, m25 n02, m39 n07) align with visible source noteheads and staff positions but remain flagged for a second manual check.

A printed “A Viol. I.” cue indication is visible in system 3. Reduced heads there are tagged cue, but the cue’s exact start/end among adjacent full-size Horn II heads should be reviewed before whole-part playback.
Reduced heads outside that labeled span are tagged cue_candidate rather than silently treated as Horn II notes.
MusicXML duration_quarters remain provisional OMR candidates. The original rhythm glyphs are preserved in the source page; a separate rhythm-by-rhythm pass is still needed for playback-grade timing.
Treble clef with 8 below begins at measure 37; the combined builder must apply the octave semantics consistently when computing concert-pitch octaves.
